summary: Two wooden range beacons that guided ships into Nantucket Harbor from 1838 or 1839; the towers stand privately on Pawguvnet Lane.

access.note: Privately owned; grounds and towers closed (LighthouseFriends). Not open to the public (Town of Nantucket).

events.note: Two beacons being erected at the head of Brant Point (Carpender's 1838 inspection as LighthouseFriends reports it).
Peleg Easton hired as the first keeper that year; the Town and Preservation Trust also date the beacons to 1838 or 1839.
Front beacon rebuilt and rear beacon raised.
Wooden pyramidal towers replaced by the conical wooden towers still standing; brick oil house added the same year.
Discontinued 14 July 1908 (LighthouseFriends); Preservation Trust says decommissioned in 1908; Town's page ends service in 1907.
Discontinued front light and keeper's tool house sold to Ellenwood B. Coleman.
Frank B. Gilbreth, Sr. bought the property from the Coleman estate for $1,840.

Taller tower moved by horse to the Gilbreth lot. No year is given for the move. The Preservation Trust mentions it beside the larger cottage that replaced the toolhouse by 1952; LighthouseFriends places the tower just abaft the cottage it dates to 1952 and prints Frank Jr.'s memory of the day at age ten. The year shown is the cottage date, not a dated move.
Listed in the Light-House Board's 1899 index as light stations 149 and 150, Nantucket Cliff.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Our record gives 1912 (Wikidata and Rowlett). LighthouseFriends gives the discontinuance as 14 July 1908, and the Preservation Trust says 1908; 1912 is the year the discontinued front light and tool house were sold. The Town's page gives 1907.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the USLHS place record for the rear light has no roster. The nine principal keepers come from the record for the front light of the pair (archives.uslhs.org/places/nantucket-cliff-range-front), which the story treats as covering both. Names after 1852 are the archive's and are not confirmed in a primary register. Dates: the Town's page (1839-1907), the Preservation Trust (1908), LighthouseFriends (14 July 1908) and our record (1912, the sale) disagree; the story says so. Gilbreth children: LighthouseFriends says eleven, the Preservation Trust twelve. The move of the taller tower has no year in any source: LighthouseFriends places it just abaft the cottage it dates to 1952 and prints Frank Jr.'s memory from age ten; the Preservation Trust mentions it beside the cottage built by 1952. The earlier draft's 'soon after 1921' was not in LighthouseFriends. Not reached: the gilbreths.com essay on the Bug Lights (DNS failure); the USCG Historian's article on the Nantucket range lights (archived copies returned no readable text). Newspapers: a Chronicling America search for Cliff Range and Nantucket, Massachusetts papers 1880-1925, returned no hits. Corpus: the cached Lighthouse Board text (1891-1901) has no body entries for the Cliff pair; the only corpus evidence is the 1899 index (scan page 91, OCR 'Nantncket Cliff'). The 1842 Easton report and the 1838 inspection are known only through LighthouseFriends. Names of current owners are left out, as the guide asks for private residents of converted lights. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the opening now gives 1838 or 1839 (the Town says 1839); the 1842 report's 151 gallons is for both beacons together; the 1899 index entry was re-read on scan page 91; the USLHS rear-light roster claim in these notes was not re-checked.
